subject: Upgrade conductor runbook and network gating assignments
messages:

Cc: ops@acmeanalytics.com

Subject: Upgrade conductor runbook and network gating assignments

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. We're planning a coordinated upgrade of our private deployment (on-prem cluster) that will touch version pinning, network gating (BGP and firewall rules), and the KV cache migration you discussed with Monica last week. High level ask: can Redwood provide a single runbook we can follow that includes the network gating table and the owner assignments for each step?

Constraints:
- Maintenance window requested: Nov 6, 02:00-06:00 UTC (we can move if Redwood needs local-business-hours coverage).
- We need a clearly documented rollback path that can be executed within 30 minutes if token RPC error rates spike above 2% after canary.
- Compliance will want a one-page audit summary after the run.

I've attached a draft list of network CIDRs and the ops contact matrix (ops@acmeanalytics.com). Please send over a runbook and tell us who from Redwood will be the on-call owner during the window.

Attachments: network-cidrs.xlsx (referenced), ops-contact-matrix.csv

Jared
Infrastructure Lead
Acme Analytics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Upgrade conductor runbook and network gating assignments

Thanks Jared — copied the core ops folks on our side. We can own the runbook and the 'conductor' role on the day of the window. Quick answers up-front:

- Maintenance window: Nov 6 02:00-06:00 UTC is acceptable for our on-call rotation.
- Canary plan: we'll run a 30-minute canary on a single availability segment (10% traffic) with health gates: 95th p90 latency <= baseline+40ms, error rate < 1.0%, and KV miss rate within historical variance.
- Rollback: a documented pin-and-revert procedure (we'll snapshot the pinned-version map and provide a one-command revert). Aim is <= 30 minutes to full rollback for control-plane-only failures; data-plane rollback (BGP) may require coordination with your netops.

Attached: initial runbook (upgrade-conductor-runbook-v1.pdf) and a net gate ownership spreadsheet (net-gate-assignments.xlsx). Please review the owner column — Monica and Naomi are the internal owners for version gating and KV cache respectively; Aditya will be the network liaison for the BGP changes.

Action items for Acme before Nov 6:
- Confirm the CIDR list in your spreadsheet (ops@acmeanalytics.com) and provide a standing firewall rule change window for test CIDRs.
- Provide a single point-of-contact on-site for BGP changes and a waypoint to open/close the session (we'll coordinate on Slack).

I'll be the conductor during the window (phone available). If that works, we'll iterate the runbook and schedule a 45-minute dry run with your team the week prior.

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, On-Prem Operations
Redwood Inference

On Wed, Oct 28, 2026 at 11:04 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached: initial runbook (upgrade-conductor-runbook-v1.pdf) and a net gate ownership spreadsheet.

Quick technical notes / runbook highlights so we have a common baseline:

1) Version pinning strategy:
   - We'll implement a per-tenant pin map stored in the control plane (snapshot before window). Pin map format documented in the runbook (pinned_version, timestamp, pinned_by).
   - Canary uses pinned_variant=v1.9-canary; rollback is revert-to-last-snapshot which automates the pin-map replacement and signals all edge nodes to drop new KV and rehydrate.

2) KV cache and migration risks:
   - During the upgrade we will disable aggressive KV prefetch for 20 minutes post-cut to avoid thundering herd on backend.
   - After pin is applied, we'll monitor KV miss-rate and backend QPS. If KV miss-rate > 3x baseline for two consecutive 5-min buckets, we trigger stage-1 rollback (reapply previous pin and drain the canary segment).

3) Network gating and BGP choreography (Aditya):
   - Planned BGP session switch at T+40 minutes after canary starts to give the control-plane a stable state.
   - Net gate spreadsheet maps each temporary ACL change to a rollback ACL. Please ensure Acme's firewall appliance supports a quick revert API; if not, document manual steps.

4) Communication and audit:
   - Post-run one-page audit template included in appendix A of the runbook; ops must confirm who signs it.

I'll add a short checklist for the dry run (smoke tests, canary metric baselines, quick revert commands). Happy to join your dry run meeting — propose Nov 2 at 14:00 UTC.

— Monica
Sr. Product Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
